LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers 1.1 Number Concept (8 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner
Topic 1.2: Whole Numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Whole Numbers, part of Numbers 1.1 Number Concept (8 lessons) By the end of the sub strand, the learner in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we get the next number in a number pattern?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Count numbers forward up to 100 starting from any point, orally/ by pointing/ placing counters or using alternative modes of communication to carry out the activity.

2. Count numbers backward from 50 starting from any point.

3. Recognize and read numbers 1 to 100 in symbols from number cards or charts.

4. Name and write the numbers in the place value of ones and tens, tens on charts/ value notation tables in exercise worksheets or in their adapted digital devices using appropriate assistive technology for writing/ stamping. Learners with difficulties in manipulation

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Count numbers forward up to 100 starting from any point, orally/ by pointing/ placing counters or using alternative modes of communication to carry out the activity.
2. Count numbers backward from 50 starting from any point.
3. Recognize and read numbers 1 to 100 in symbols from number cards or charts.
4. Name and write the numbers in the place value of ones and tens, tens on charts/ value notation tables in exercise worksheets or in their adapted digital devices using appropriate assistive technology for writing/ stamping. Learners with difficulties in manipulation

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Whole Numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learner improvises place value tins and pockets from locally available materials.

● Communication and collaboration: learner discusses the place value of digits written on the number cards.
